cards.text: We're with Jeremiah, a prophet carrying the LORD's message, friend. He just spent a long stretch on idols that can't even walk (Jeremiah 10:5). Now he turns to the people of the land, living under siege with the enemy right outside their walls.

cards.question: The people living under siege get their first order. What are they told to do?

answers.text: Gather up their belongings from the land
Rebuild the walls around their city
Open the gates to the enemy army

cards.text: Pack your bags. Friend, when they slid me into that junk drawer, I didn't get to pack ONE thing! Then the LORD says why: He's going to sling the people of the land right out of it.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll sling the people out of the land someday, far off in the future.
The LORD says He'll bring distress on the people of the land so that they may be ___.

cards.text: Then the speaker cries out, and it gets personal: "Woe to me because of my brokenness; my wound is grievous!"

cards.question: Right after crying woe over that wound, what does the speaker say about it?

answers.text: It is my sickness and I must bear it
Someone else caused it and must fix it
It will heal on its own before long

cards.text: Now the picture is a tent. The speaker's tent is destroyed, and ALL its ropes are snapped. Not one rope, friend. ALL of them.

cards.question: With the tent destroyed, the speaker's sons are still close by, ready to help put it back up.
With the sons gone and the tent torn down, who's left to pitch it again and set up the curtains?

cards.text: So how did it get this bad? The speaker points at the shepherds: they've become senseless, and they do not seek the LORD. That's a tour guide who REFUSES to look at the map.

cards.question: Because the shepherds don't seek the LORD, they have not prospered, and all their ___ is scattered.

cards.text: Then, LISTEN! The sound of a report is coming, a great commotion, the kind of noise that makes you freeze in bed at 2 a.m.

cards.question: Where is this great commotion coming from?
When the commotion arrives, the cities of Judah will be left full and thriving.

cards.text: Judah's cities will be a desolation, a haunt for jackals. When the jackals move in, friend, that neighborhood is NOT on the way up.
Then the speaker turns from the warning and talks straight to the LORD. And what he says is about who's really in charge of a person's path.

cards.question: Talking straight to the LORD, the speaker says he knows that no one who walks directs his own steps.

cards.text: Then the speaker asks the LORD for correction. On PURPOSE. Friend, I flinch when somebody just says, "Can I give you a little feedback?"

cards.question: How does the speaker ask the LORD to correct him?

answers.text: Only with justice and not in anger
Quickly so that it will soon be over
Privately and away from the people

cards.question: The speaker says that correction in the LORD's anger would ___ him.

cards.text: Then the prayer turns toward the nations that do not acknowledge the LORD, the families that do not call on His name.

cards.question: The speaker asks the LORD to pour out His ___ on the nations that do not acknowledge Him.
Why does the speaker ask the LORD to pour out wrath on those nations?

cards.text: The prayer calls God's people Jacob, after the man whose sons became the tribes of Israel (Genesis 49:28). Those nations have consumed him, finished him off and devastated his homeland.
